subject: In Pursuit Of The Largest IPO In History
body_text:
Good morning! Here's the latest in trending:$7B quarterly loss: Spotlight on SoftBank's (SFTBY) massive AI spending.New MoU: Exxon (XOM) eyes Venezuelan oil despite calling nation 'uninvestable.'Despite tariffs: China's trade surplus surges past $1T for the second year in a row.

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 $7B quarterly loss: Spotlight on SoftBank's ( SFTBY ) massive AI spending . 

New MoU: Exxon ( XOM ) eyes Venezuelan oil despite calling nation 'uninvestable.' 

 Despite tariffs: China's trade surplus surges past $1T for the second year in a row.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Claude’s biggest prompt 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 All eyes are on Anthropic ( ANT ) now that the 15-day waiting period following its initial S-1 filing has come to an end. It means that the company behind Claude can now begin marketing its much-anticipated initial public offering. It wants to be the largest IPO in history, breaking the record of SpaceX ( SPCX ), which went public only six months ago. The question is—whether it can. Anthropic to begin trading next week 

 Snapshot: The midterms brought some violent swings to AI-related shares amid an already-volatile environment for tech stocks and rising interest rates. There have been fears over the rapid buildout of data centers used to train and run AI models, especially with initiatives on the ballot in many regions and a Democratic sweep that'll likely bring more AI safety regulation. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has even called on top AI firms to slow the development pace of their most advanced models, but pausing may simply be a luxury no frontier lab can afford. Upgraded versions of Fable and Mythos released 

Given that backdrop, Anthropic's valuation continues to change, at least according to reports, and will likely end up raising $80B-$100B at a valuation of $1.25T-$1.75T. Regarding the financials, the company's revenue has jumped ten-fold over the past year to $16.3B, but so has its costs, with a net loss of $80.7B. While those numbers are staggering, Anthropic needs to spend big to compete in the AI arms race, as it faces off against well-capitalized firms like Google ( GOOGL ), Meta ( META ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ), as well as OpenAI ( OPENAI ), which is also in the battle to soon go public. Anthropic IPO details sent by mistake 

 Outlook: Market analysts increasingly argue that the way Anthropic trades will help decide the AI revolution's ultimate winners and losers. While it will definitely be an influential bellwether for market valuations, there is a lot more to the AI technology stack than this one dominant name. Those include semiconductor designers, memory suppliers, advanced packaging foundries and energy providers. Their economics depend on aggregate industry demand for compute, regardless of whether Claude ends up taking the cake, or ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok become formidable rivals. The Anthropic Feedback Loop: The Cost Of Capital Delusion And Diversion

What else is happening...
 
 
 
 WSB survey results: Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Huang likely to remain in the top spot .

... affair allegedly helped facilitate $7.5B in chip shipments to China .

Lilly ( LLY ), Novo ( NVO ) weight-loss drugs to get rare vision loss warning .

Take-Two ( TTWO ) says GTA VI preorders are at 'unprecedented' levels .

Michael Burry trims Caterpillar ( CAT ) bearish bet as puts nearly quadruple .

Goldman ( GS ) CEO: AI financing demand is still strong despite tech selloff .

Hims & Hers ( HIMS ) declines following double miss, lowered guidance .

Boeing ( BA ) to cut commercial aircraft staff as it slows output ramp-up . 

PepsiCo ( PEP ) reshapes North American business with 1,000 job cuts .

Amazon ( AMZN ) sets 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Week plans .


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Today's Markets
 
 
 
 In Asia, Japan +2.9% . Hong Kong +0.4% . China +0.1% . India +0.1% .
 In Europe, at midday, London +0.5% . Paris +1.1% . Frankfurt +1.2% .
 Futures at 6:30, Dow +0.3% . S&P +0.1% . Nasdaq -0.2% . Crude -1.1% to $85.86. Gold -0.8% to $4,082.50. Bitcoin -0.4% to $74,131.
 Ten-year Treasury Yield unchanged at  4.90%.
 
 
 
 
On The Calendar
 
 
 
 Companies reporting today include CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Rigetti Computing ( RGTI ).
